title: ACTS College Student Handbook 2025-2026

sections.title: DISCIPLINARY PROCEDURES
sections.content: The ACTS Student Handbook outlines clear disciplinary procedures for maintaining academic integrity and student conduct. All disciplinary actions must follow the progressive discipline approach.

sections.title: CATEGORY 1 OFFENSES - MINOR VIOLATIONS
sections.content: Category 1 offenses include minor behavioral issues such as tardiness, minor uniform violations, and small classroom disruptions. Sanctions for first offense: Verbal Warning. Second offense: Written Warning. Third offense: Written Warning with Counseling. Multiple offenses: Detention (1 day) or Written Warning + Counseling.

sections.title: CATEGORY 2 OFFENSES - MODERATE VIOLATIONS
sections.content: Category 2 offenses include cheating on minor assignments, disrespectful behavior toward peers, and unauthorized use of school facilities. First offense: Written Warning + Parent Conference. Repeat offenses: Suspension (1-3 days) with behavior contract and counseling.

sections.title: CATEGORY 3 OFFENSES - MAJOR VIOLATIONS
sections.content: Category 3 offenses include academic dishonesty (cheating on exams), physical altercations, vandalism, and possession of prohibited items. Sanctions: Suspension (3-5 days) + Mandatory Counseling. Severe cases may result in expulsion proceedings.

sections.title: PROGRESSIVE DISCIPLINE POLICY
sections.content: ACTS follows a progressive discipline approach: 1) Verbal Warning, 2) Written Warning, 3) Detention/Counseling, 4) Suspension, 5) Expulsion. Each disciplinary action considers the student's history, circumstances, and willingness to improve.

sections.title: COUNSELING REQUIREMENTS
sections.content: Students receiving disciplinary sanctions may be required to attend counseling sessions. Counseling focuses on behavior modification, conflict resolution, and personal development. Parents are involved in counseling plans for serious offenses.

sections.title: PARENTAL INVOLVEMENT
sections.content: Parents must be notified for all Category 2 and 3 offenses. Parent conferences are mandatory for repeated offenses and serious violations. Parent acknowledgment is required for disciplinary action plans.

sections.title: APPEALS PROCESS
sections.content: Students may appeal disciplinary decisions within 3 school days. Appeals are heard by the Student Disciplinary Committee. The committee reviews evidence, student statements, and mitigating circumstances before making final decisions.
